task_retrieval_key:
A 9-year-old Chinese girl presenting with symptoms since birth. The patient has thickened nails, keratinized plaques on palms, soles, and corners of the mouth. At age 1, her fingernails and toenails began to turn yellow and thicken. The skin of stressed parts of palms and soles gradually became keratinized, thickened, black and chapped. No family history of similar symptoms. Physical examination showed normal vision, hearing, intelligence, and growth, with moderate nutrition.
- Nail examination: Fingernails and toenails partly thickened and raised in wedge shape, surface rough, opaque, and dirty brown
- Skin examination: Dry skin on trunk and extremities; punctate and flaky keratinized dark brown thickened patches on palms and soles
- Oral examination: Fissured tongue, oral leukokeratosis, and keratotic plaques in corners of mouth
- No natal teeth, follicular sebaceous cysts, hair loss, or other organ abnormalities
